questions.stem_text: Find the order of the factor group Z_6/<3>.
questions.answer_explanation: The order of the factor group Z_6/<3> is 3 because the subgroup <3> consists of the elements {0, 3} in Z_6, and the factor group is formed by the cosets of this subgroup, which results in three distinct cosets: {0, 3}, {1, 4}, and {2, 5}.

Let A be the set of all ordered pairs of integers (m, n) such that 7 m + 12 n = 22. What
is the greatest negative number in the set B = {m + n : (m, n) \in A}?
questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer is -4 because the equation 7m + 12n = 22 can be rearranged to express n in terms of m, and by substituting integer values for m, the maximum value of m+n that is negative occurs at m = -4 and n = 0, yielding m+n = -4.

questions.stem_text:
There is an unlimited supply of congruent equilateral triangles made of colored paper.
Each triangle is a solid color with the same color on both sides of the paper. A large
equilateral triangle is constructed from four of these paper triangles as shown. Two large
triangles are considered distinguishable if it is not possible to place one on the other,
using translations, rotations, and/or reflections, so that their corresponding small
triangles are of the same color. Given that there are six different colors of triangles
from which to choose, how many distinguishable large equilateral triangles can be
constructed? [asy] draw((0,0)--(10,0)--(5,8.7)--cycle);
draw((5,0)--(2.5,4.3)--(7.5,4.3)--cycle); [/asy]
questions.gold_answer:
Because any permutation of the vertices of a large triangle can be obtained by rotation or
reflection, the coloring of the large triangle is determined by which set of three colors
is used for the corner triangles and the color that is used for the center triangle. If
the three corner triangles are the same color, there are six possible sets of colors for
them. If exactly two of the corner triangles are the same color, there are $6\cdot 5=30$
possible sets of colors. If the three corner triangles are different colors, there are
${6\choose 3}=20$ possible sets of colors. Therefore there are $6+30+20=56$ sets of colors
for the corner triangles. Because there are six choices for the color of the center
triangle, there are $6\cdot 56=\boxed{336}$ distinguishable triangles.
questions.answer_explanation: correct because it accurately accounts for the distinct color combinations of the corner and center triangles by considering the effects of symmetry through rotations and reflections, leading to a systematic enumeration of distinguishable configurations based on the equality and inequality of colors among the corner triangles.

questions.stem_text:
Find all values of $x$ such that \[ \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ x & 7 & -2 \\ x^3 & 343 &
-8 \end{vmatrix} = 0.\]Enter your values separated by commas. For example, if you think
the possible values are 4, 5, and 6, then enter you answer as "4,5,6".
questions.gold_answer:
Subtracting the second column from the first column, we get \[ \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1
\\ x - 7 & 7 & -2 \\ x^3 - 343 & 343 & -8 \end{vmatrix} = 0.\]The first column becomes all
zeros when $x = 7,$ so this is one possible value of $x.$ Subtracting the third column
from the first column, we get \[ \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 \\ x + 2 & 7 & -2 \\ x^3 + 8 &
343 & -8 \end{vmatrix} = 0.\]The first column becomes all zeros when $x = -2,$ so this is
another possible value of $x.$ Expanding the last determinant along the first column, we
get \begin{align*} \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 \\ x + 2 & 7 & -2 \\ x^3 + 8 & 343 & -8
\end{vmatrix} &= -(x + 2) \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 343 & -8 \end{vmatrix} + (x^3 + 8)
\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 7 & -2 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= -9 x^3 + 351 x + 630 = 0.
\end{align*}Since we know that $x = 7$ are $x = -2$ are two solutions, we can take out a
factor of $x - 7$ and $x + 2$, to get \[-9(x - 7)(x + 2)(x + 5) = 0.\]Hence, the possible
values of $x$ are $\boxed{7, -2, \text{ and } -5}.$ (Alternatively, by Vieta's formulas,
the sum of the three roots of $-9 x^3 + 351 x + 630 = 0$ is 0, so the third root is $-7 -
(-2) = -5.$)
questions.answer_explanation: correct because it demonstrates the application of column operations on determinants, revealing specific values of \(x\) that lead to a column of zeros, which indicates that the determinant is zero, thus satisfying the original equation.
